title: An-Nazi'at: fear of standing
hookLine: whoever feared standing before his Lord and held the self from desire, the garden is home (79:40–41)

lines: ELEVEN AT NIGHT, PHONE IN HAND.
THE GAP BETWEEN WANTING AND DOING.
WHERE THE SURAH ENDS ITS ARGUMENT.
cards: It's eleven at night. The phone is in your hand, and the thumb already knows the way. One more video.
A second slice. The reply you'd regret by morning, typed and waiting for the send button. That tiny gap between wanting something and doing it is so small that most days it goes unnoticed.
Three days into An-Nazi'at, the surah ends its argument inside exactly that gap.
After the great upheaval and the story of Musa and Pharaoh, it sorts people into two, and the second group is known by what they did in that small moment.

teach.b: First the other group: whoever rebelled and chose the life of this world, the fire is home.
Then the turn, in Pickthall's words: But as for him who feared to stand before his Lord and restrained his soul from lust, Lo! the Garden will be his home. Two things.

teach.h: MAQAM — THE STANDING BEFORE HIS LORD.
teach.b: The first is a fear, and a specific one: maqam rabbihi, the standing before his Lord. Commentators read it two ways. Some say it means the Day when every person will stand before Allah to give an account.
Others say it means Allah standing over a person now, seeing what they do in the dark. Either way, it's the awareness of being seen, like a light switched on in a room.
The second thing is the holding: the soul, the nafs, held back from al-hawa.

teach.h: HAWA — THE SELF BLOWN BY WHIM.
teach.b: Pickthall says lust, but hawa is wider: the pull of whim, the wind that blows the self wherever it likes. Notice what's not said. The verse doesn't condemn wanting.
It names the self steered only by the wind.

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ put it in a picture Bukhari records: the strong one isn't the wrestler who throws people down; the strong one controls himself when angry. And one small word at the end: home. Not reward, not prize.
The Garden is where this person lives.
That closes An-Nazi'at; tomorrow, one surah back, to An-Naba'.

how: Muslims describe this as struggle with the self (jihad an-nafs): fasting, lowering the gaze, and holding the tongue in anger are all practiced as small, daily ways of restraining the self from whim.

o: the surah named for those who pull out
the surah named for those who plant seeds
the surah named for those who build houses

games.q: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.
p: whim, the pull of the self

s: the surah says every desire is sinful
it names hawa, the self steered by whim, not wanting as such.
commentators read the standing before his Lord in more than one way
the Day of account, or Allah standing over a person now.
the Prophet said the strong one is the best wrestler
Bukhari: the strong one controls himself when angry.

games.q: the surah sorts people into two. what marks the second group?
o: they feared the standing and held the self back
they gave up the world completely
games.why: 79:40–41: they feared to stand before their Lord and restrained the self from whim. the desire was there; they held it.

practice: Pick one small desire you already know will come today, the snack at four, the extra hour of scrolling, the sharp reply, and picture the half second before you act.

Stay in that gap and breathe slowly, letting it widen a little; nothing is being taken from you, you're only noticing that you can choose. If you pray, bring to mind the standing before your Lord as you breathe.

wordCard.voice: An-Nazi'at. Those who pull out, the surah that ends by sorting people by what they did with the gap: the ones who held the self back from whim. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: whim, the self's pull. 79:40 speaks of holding the nafs back from it.

carryVoice: Your line: hold the self back. The wanting can stay; the wind doesn't have to steer. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: But as for him who feared to stand before his Lord and restrained his soul from lust, Lo! the Garden will be his home.

sources.ref: Qur'an 79:37–39 (the one who rebelled and chose the life of the world)
